text:
If you're heading out for a sunset stroll tonight, you're in good shape: skies are clear now, clouds build in through the evening, and it stays mild with a low around 63. Light south wind, nothing to plan around.

Tomorrow's the one to watch. Sunshine and building humidity push highs into the mid-80s, and that's the fuel for afternoon and evening thunderstorms, some capable of strong winds and heavy rain, mainly rolling through between 4 and 8pm. The forecasters' confidence in a few stronger storms has actually gone up since this morning, and the European model is notably wetter than the American guidance, so I'd lean toward believing the storm risk over hoping it fizzles. The lake will be up too, south wind 15 to 25 knots and waves building to 2 to 3 feet, so plan any boating for the morning and be off the water well before early afternoon. By Friday things calm down fast with lingering showers fading into a beautiful start to the weekend.
